title: "Circular (Circos-style) multi-track plots in R with canvasXpress"
description: "Draw a circular genome plot in R — stacked data tracks around a ring with connection ribbons — from one portable spec."
author: "Isaac Neuhaus"
date: "2026-10-23"

A circular (Circos-style) plot wraps a genome — or any ordered set of segments — into a ring, stacks
several **data tracks** around it, and draws **ribbons** for relationships between positions. In R
the reference is `circlize`. Here we build an interactive one with
[canvasXpress](https://canvasxpress.org), from a single portable spec.

## The data shape

The matrix is **tracks × segments** (rows are the tracks you draw, columns are the positions around
the ring). A sample annotation segments the ring (here into chromosomes), and `circularConnections`
is a list of `[colour, from, to]` ribbons.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(canvasXpress)

set.seed(8)
segments <- paste0("s", 1:80)
tracks   <- c("Expression", "Methylation", "CopyNumber", "Density")
y <- matrix(round(rnorm(length(tracks) * length(segments)), 2),
            nrow = length(tracks), dimnames = list(tracks, segments))

smpAnnot <- data.frame(Region = rep(paste0("chr", 1:4), each = 20), row.names = segments)

cols  <- c("rgb(220,40,40)", "rgb(40,120,220)", "rgb(40,160,60)", "rgb(240,150,20)")
conns <- lapply(1:18, function(i)
  list(sample(cols, 1), sample(segments, 1), sample(segments, 1)))
```

## The plot

`circularTrackGraphType` picks a renderer per track (`bar`, `heatmap`, `line`, `dot`),
`circularTrackGraphWeight` sets each track's radial thickness, and `segregateSamplesBy` splits the
ring by the annotation.

```{r}
canvasXpress(
  data      = y, smpAnnot = smpAnnot,
  graphType = "Circular",
  circularConnections     = conns,
  circularTrackGraphType  = list("bar", "heatmap", "line", "dot"),
  circularTrackGraphWeight = list(30, 20, 25, 25),
  circularTrackName        = list(1, 2, 3, 4),
  segregateSamplesBy       = list("Region"),
  title     = "Circos-style multi-track plot with connections",
  width     = 560, height = 560
)
```

Each ring is one track; the inner ribbons are the connections. Hover a segment to read its values;
swap the matrix and ribbons for your own genomic tracks and interactions.

## Why "reproducible"

The matrix, the connections and the `config` **are** the figure — one portable spec. The same spec
renders the identical circular plot from Python or JavaScript, and can be validated and re-rendered
later.
